content: {"claims":[{"quote":"The grade is deterministic and rests on three published rules: the proof rule (a claim without a trace never earns more than C; missing information is shown as unknown and caps the grade at C), the weakest link (the final grade is the worst answer) and a dated, tamper-evident seal (commit, method version, SHA-256 fingerprint, 90-day expiry).","topic":"verifiability"},{"quote":"Apertus does what fixed rules cannot: it extracts what a project claims about itself, sets each claim against the traces and names the contradictions, and writes the verdict in German, French, Italian and Romansh. Every Apertus answer is checked against the evidence before use, and rejections are counted in the report.","topic":"verifiability"},{"quote":"Applied to the 26 public Hugging Face Spaces that use Apertus (aggregated, anonymous), no project reaches A or B; 42 % call the model through a foreign service and 73 % ship telemetry on by default.","topic":"third_party_services"},{"quote":"Sigillum examined itself first: D on its first run (no licence file in the project folder), A after the fix, with its limits published.","topic":"model_location|data_flow|offline"},{"quote":"The architecture runs on one machine, no outbound network.","topic":"offline"}]}
